topic: Ocean facts: Greenland shark age, Challenger Deep, brine pools, ocean oxygen, unmapped seafloor
hook: Ocean facts that sound made up
caption:
The ocean covers about 70% of our planet, yet only about a quarter of its floor is mapped in high detail.

Down there are sharks that may be older than the United States, lakes with their own shores, and a trench deep enough to swallow Mount Everest.

Which of these would you most want to see with your own eyes?

carousel_caption:
The ocean covers about 70% of our planet, yet only about a quarter of its floor is mapped in high detail.

Down there are sharks that may be older than the United States, lakes with their own shores, and a trench deep enough to swallow Mount Everest.

Which of these would you most want to see with your own eyes?

Cover: Ocean facts that sound made up
📷 Bureau of Ocean Energy Management/United States Department of the Interior (Public domain) via wikimedia

1/5 A 400-year-old shark (400)
Greenland sharks may live around 400 years. Some swimming today could be older than the United States.
📷 Hemming1952 (CC BY-SA 4.0) via wikimedia

2/5 Everest would vanish (11 km)
The Challenger Deep is about 10,900 m deep. Drop Everest in and its peak stays 2 km underwater.
🎨 AI-generated image

3/5 Lakes under the sea
In the Gulf of Mexico, super-salty brine pools sit on the seafloor, with their own shores and even waves.
📷 Image courtesy of the NOAA Office of Ocean Exploration and Research. (Public domain) via wikimedia

4/5 Half your oxygen (50%)
Tiny ocean plankton make about half the oxygen on Earth. Roughly every other breath comes from the sea.
📷 Prof. Gordon T. Taylor, Stony Brook University (Public domain) via wikimedia

5/5 Mostly unmapped (25%)
Only about a quarter of the seafloor is mapped in high detail. The rest is still a blur.
📷 NASA Earth Observatory images by Wanmei Liang, using Landsat data from the U.S.  (Public domain) via wikimedia
